title.suggested: Tom Allen in New York for a Benefit and the Rooke Match

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Democrat reprinted a New York Sun account of Tom Allen's visit to New York, his benefit at Harry Hill's, and his coming $3,000 fight with George Rooke near Pittsburg on June 17.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'The St. Louis Democrat: St. Louis, Tuesday, March 16, 1875' (before the May 1875 merger).

facts.fact: Allen was matched to fight George Rooke for $3,000 within fifty miles of Pittsburg on June 17, 1875; the second deposit of $250 a side was made with stakeholder Harry Hill
Allen arrived in Newark, met Jim Coyne, then went on to New York as Harry Hill's guest, visiting Billy Edwards in Brooklyn
Allen planned a sparring tour: a week at Mortimer's Theater in Philadelphia, then Pittsburg, Cleveland, Detroit, Toledo and Chicago, before returning home to St. Louis to train
A benefit for Allen was held at Harry Hill's Variety Theater in New York, where he sparred Jim Coyne in the main bout
places: Harry Hill's Variety Theater, New York

facts.fact: Allen said he weighed 210 pounds and had to train off forty pounds before the Rooke fight
facts.quote: There is one thing, my friend, that I want you to print, and that is that I now weigh only 210 pounds. That is bad enough, but some of the papers have got me down for 240. As it is, I have got to train off forty pounds before I have my fight with Rooke, for I never fight at over 170.

facts.fact: Allen showed a gold and silver championship belt inscribed 'Presented to Tom Allen by his St. Louis friends, May 4, 1870'
The Sun gave Allen's birth as Birmingham, 1840, and listed his fight record in England and America

notes: Belt date May 4, 1870 differs from fact 021 (April 29, 1870); birth year 1840 differs from fact 001 (1839).
